- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) after a recent spike, model should not overshoot downward — cap decline to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- Forecast mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if model shows persistent upward trend beyond 10–15 days, adjust downward by 2–5% per week.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model should not overfit to recent momentum — dampen forecast slope by 10–20% if recent 7-day avg is flat.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to correct for overconfidence bias.  
- For sentiment history with high volatility (alternating +/– 0.3+), model should smooth out extreme swings — avoid forecasting 3–5% jumps unless sentiment confirms.
